stories.headline: NVIDIA Q1 REVENUE HITS RECORD $81.6B, SMASHING ESTIMATES AS AI DEMAND SHOWS NO CEILING
stories.body: Nvidia's Q1 FY27 results blew past the $79.2B consensus, with data center revenue alone at $75.2B (+92% YoY) and EPS of $1.87 vs. $1.78 expected; despite the beat, shares fell ~1.4% as Q2 guidance of $91B implied the AI-driven supercycle is already priced in by a market that has rewarded the stock 20% YTD.

stories.headline: DOW SETS FRESH ALL-TIME HIGH AT 50,579 AS S&P 500 NOTCHES EIGHTH STRAIGHT WINNING WEEK
stories.body: The Dow climbed 294 points to a new record close Friday, capping the S&P 500's longest winning streak in more than two years; risk appetite held despite oil near $100 and yields at 4.54%, with markets pricing a soft-landing scenario where Nvidia-led earnings offset geopolitical headwinds heading into the long weekend.

stories.headline: IRAN'S SUPREME LEADER BLOCKS URANIUM DEAL — WTI REBOUNDS TO $97 WITH $100 IN SIGHT
stories.body: Ayatollah Khamenei ordered that Iran's enriched uranium stay within the country, undercutting a draft U.S.-Iran framework that had briefly cooled oil markets; WTI rebounded to $97.29/bbl after pulling back from $100 resistance, and gold slipped to ~$4,490 as risk appetite remained cautious — the Strait of Hormuz supply risk stays live.

stories.headline: FINAL MICHIGAN CONSUMER SENTIMENT OUT TODAY; HOUSING DATA TOPPED CONSENSUS THIS WEEK
stories.body: The final May University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment reading released today offers the Fed's clearest signal on whether consumers are anchoring higher inflation expectations — a 5-10Y expectation above 3.2% would shift June dot-plot language; separately, housing data beat consensus even as 30-year mortgage rates held near 6.8%, suggesting demand is more resilient than rates imply.

stories.headline: MICHIGAN RELOADS FOR 2026-27; FLORIDA, DUKE LEAD WAY-TOO-EARLY RANKINGS AS PORTAL RESHAPES ROSTERS
stories.body: Defending champion Michigan added three frontcourt transfers (Moustapha Thiam, J.P. Estrella, Jalen Reed) to its title-winning core, while Florida vaulted to No. 1 in early 2026-27 polls after Thomas Haugh and Alex Condon spurned the NBA draft; the tournament expands to 76 teams next year, complicating bubble projections for mid-majors.

stories.headline: SPURS-THUNDER GAME 3 TONIGHT IN SAN ANTONIO, SERIES TIED 1-1; KNICKS UP 2-0 ON CAVALIERS
stories.body: The Western Conference Finals resume tonight at 8:30 PM ET with the Spurs hosting Oklahoma City in a pivotal Game 3 (series 1-1 after Spurs' double-OT Game 1 win and Thunder's Game 2 answer 122-113); in the East, New York leads Cleveland 2-0 and heads to Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse for Game 3 Saturday.

stories.headline: AARON RODGERS CONFIRMS 2026 IS HIS FINAL NFL SEASON WITH STEELERS AS OTAs BEGIN LEAGUE-WIDE
stories.body: Rodgers, 42, told reporters his one-year return to Pittsburgh under Mike McCarthy will be his last; in other OTA news, the Rams locked up reigning MVP Matthew Stafford through 2027 at $55M annually, while the Giants lost DL Roy Robertson-Harris to a torn Achilles and GM Joe Schoen signed a multi-year extension.

stories.headline: 100 DAYS TO KICKOFF: BIG TEN LEADS SPRING WITH 8 NEW STARTING QBS, CFP EXPANSION TALKS INTENSIFY
stories.body: The 2026 college football season is exactly 100 days away, with the Big Ten generating the most roster turnover — eight teams enter the year with new signal callers via portal and spring battles; conference commissioners are pressing hard for a 24-team CFP format, setting up a governance showdown before the 2027 season.

deepDive.title: Oil at $97, Yields at 4.54%: How the Fed Reads an Energy Shock
content: Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei delivered a stark directive Thursday: enriched uranium stays on Iranian soil, collapsing a draft U.S.-Iran framework that had briefly pushed WTI toward $90. With one statement, crude rebounded to $97 and the threat of a $100 oil shock returned — on the same day the Dow hit a new all-time high. That seeming contradiction reveals something important: markets are not betting on inflation returning unchecked; they are betting the Fed has already mapped out its response. Understanding that response mechanism is the essential context behind today's numbers.

The transmission from oil prices to monetary policy runs through two distinct channels. First, the direct CPI channel: a $10/bbl increase in WTI historically adds 0.3–0.5 percentage points to headline CPI within 3–6 months, primarily through gasoline, then freight and manufacturing inputs. Second, the demand-destruction channel: sustained high energy costs compress consumer discretionary spending, particularly for lower-income households who allocate 8–10% of income to transportation and utilities versus 3–4% for high earners. The net effect is stagflationary — headline inflation rises while growth softens — the scenario the Fed's dual mandate handles least gracefully.

The most instructive historical episode is 1973–74, when OPEC's embargo sent WTI from $3 to $12. Fed Chair Arthur Burns kept policy too accommodative, reasoning that oil inflation was transitory and supply-driven; the result was double-digit inflation that persisted for nearly a decade. In 2021–22, the Fed made a structurally similar error — initially calling energy-driven CPI 'transitory' before executing the fastest 525-bps hiking cycle in four decades. Both episodes share a common lesson: supply-side inflation becomes entrenched when consumer expectations become unanchored, and by the time the Fed can measure that transition, it is already behind.

The June FOMC meeting is 16 days away. If WTI holds above $95 through month-end, the updated dot plot will almost certainly show a shallower 2026 rate-cut path than March's projection. Today's final Michigan Consumer Sentiment print is the single most actionable data point in that context: specifically, the 5-10 year inflation expectations component. Historically, a reading above 3.2% correlates strongly with Fed language shifting more hawkish. If that number prints elevated today, combined with oil near $100, expect the market to reprice the long end — pushing 10-year yields back toward 4.7% and compressing equity multiples into the holiday weekend.
